Perfect. All the features are working. Let me create a short summary of the decisions made for the autonomous implementation:

## Summary

✅ **All three features implemented and verified:**

1. **Pagination** — `/products` endpoint supports cursor-based pagination (default, no data loss when dataset changes) with offset-based fallback (via `?offset=N`). Includes `hasMore` and `nextCursor` in responses. Sortable fields: id, sku, name, description, price, quantity, category, active, createdAt, updatedAt. Filterable fields: sku, category, active.

2. **Rate Limiting** — Per-IP rate limiter with token-bucket algorithm. Default: 60 burst capacity, 1 request/sec sustained (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_BURST` and `RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC` env vars). Returns 429 with `Retry-After` header when exceeded. Lives in-process memory; swap to Redis before multi-instance deployment.

3. **Request Logging** — Every request gets a correlation ID (generated as UUID if not provided via `x-request-id` header). All logs tagged with service name (from env var `SERVICE_NAME` or `package.json` name). Sensitive fields (Authorization headers, passwords in request body) are redacted. Logs to stdout via Pino; pipe to `pino-pretty` for human-readable output during development.

**Decisions made:**
- Cursor pagination by default (avoids skips/duplicates on data changes); offset mode available via `?offset=N` for UI pagination
- Per-IP rate limiting (single-process in-memory store; adequate for single instance)
- Correlation ID auto-generated if missing; respects inbound `x-request-id` header for trace continuity
- Sensitive request data stripped from logs (auth headers, body fields containing passwords)
- No documentation files created per instructions; code is self-documenting with inline comments

All 15 end-to-end checks pass. Run `node strata/verify.js` to re-verify at any time.
